Hi Maria — thanks for the heads up and for the context.

We can absolutely help keep the pilot usable while procurement completes. Here are two options we typically offer depending on how much runway you need:

- "Standby Hold" (recommended): pause the trial countdown and maintain access for 14 calendar days while the PO routes. Limited token allowance (sufficient for demos & smoke tests).
- "Warm Buffer": extend the trial + provide a micro credit top-up (48–120 hours of heavier testing) if the PO ETA is >10 calendar days.

If you can share the expected PO sign date, we’ll pick the right option. I can approve a standby hold from our side once procurement confirms they’re in routing and send a short acknowledgement DocuSign (no commercial terms, just one-line acceptance).

Looping in Marissa (CS) to coordinate the technical handoff and to set token limits so your engineers can keep running experiments without unexpected throttling. Sean is on copy to track this in our deal record.

I’ve attached our procurement guidance checklist — it tends to speed onboarding.

Vanessa Ortiz
